_meta.description: Default values by industry sector (textile, food, paper, chemical, foundry, etc.) and MSME-sector-wide baseline figures.

msme_classification.governing_act: MSMED Act, 2006, administered via Udyam Registration portal
msme_classification.classification_rule: Composite criterion -- a business must satisfy BOTH the investment and turnover condition to fall in a category. Same thresholds apply to manufacturing and service enterprises (only the investment measure's name changes: 'plant and machinery' for manufacturing vs 'equipment' for services).
msme_classification.note_for_existing_factories: Since the optimizer likely deals with existing factories (not new registrations), consider keeping both old and new thresholds with an effective_date field, in case a factory's self-reported figures predate the 2025 revision.

micro.description: very small workshops, artisan units, limited machinery

small.description: established manufacturing units, often dedicated production lines

medium.description: larger factories, sometimes multi-line or multi-shift operations

factory_size_by_category.floor_area_m2: GAP -- no official average factory floor area by MSME category found at national level; would need state Industrial Estate / DIC data or sector-specific industry association data.

sectors.ceramics_note: Not separately broken out in Ministry of MSME national data (Step 1) but explicitly confirmed as a biomass-relevant MSME sector by the MNRE-GIZ biomass report (Step 5) -- closes that gap.

biomass_process_heat_applicability.finding: Biomass can technically replace up to 100% of fossil fuels currently used for steam/heat generation in these MSME-dominated sectors.

sectors.distribution_by_activity_note: Trade-sector MSMEs hold roughly a third of all units; manufacturing MSMEs a slightly smaller share (NSS 2015-16 round) -- not all MSMEs are industrial/energy-consuming; the optimizer's target subset is manufacturing MSMEs only.

industrial_energy_consumption_share_pct.reconciliation_note: Use the World Bank FEEMP range (33-75%, sector-dependent) as the authoritative envelope; treat 25% as a commonly-cited average/rounding within that range.

electricity_vs_thermal_energy_split_pct.source: TERI, citing MSME-sector-wide data -- confirms process heat dominates MSME energy use

msme_sector_macro_stats.process_heat_share_note: Over 80% of MSME manufacturing sector energy demand comes from process heat (boilers, furnaces, dryers).

employment.discrepancy_note: The two figures differ by over 4x -- likely different methodologies (direct employment vs total including informal/indirect). Flag rather than silently pick one.

decarbonization_targets_niti_aayog_roadm.report: Roadmap for Green Transition of MSMEs (NITI Aayog, 21 Jan 2026)
decarbonization_targets_niti_aayog_roadm.long_run_context: Fossil fuels projected to still account for roughly one-fourth of industry energy consumption even by 2070 (NITI Aayog Feb 2026 follow-up), to be managed via carbon capture and other technologies -- the optimizer should not assume 100% fossil-fuel elimination as the realistic long-run end-state.
decarbonization_targets_niti_aayog_roadm.implementation_approach: Cluster-based (validated across NITI Aayog and CEEW sources) rather than treating each factory in isolation.
decarbonization_targets_niti_aayog_roadm.external_pressure_driver: EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) -- adds competitive pressure for export-oriented MSMEs (e.g. textiles) to decarbonize regardless of domestic subsidy availability.

list: disproportionately high cost of capital for MSMEs specifically
financing_barriers.behavioral_barrier: 42% of smaller manufacturing enterprises avoid third-party sustainability audits due to limited budgets and lack of direct financial incentive -- relevant to why MSMEs under-adopt even cost-effective measures.
financing_barriers.structural_finding: Cost is often the binding constraint on MSME decarbonisation more than technical/organizational readiness (CEEW steel cluster study, 2026) -- readiness is not always the bottleneck.

foundry_dri_sector_case_study.cost_structure_finding: Initial capital required is highest for CCUS and Renewable Energy deployment; CCUS and imported-coal-use switching have the highest operating expenses -- capex-heavy and opex-heavy levers should be modeled distinctly.

category_II_2_to_15_tph.confidence: not confirmed current -- may also have been revised

categories: Red (highly polluting, ~70+ sectors, mandatory CTE+CTO, often EIA/CEMS)
White (non-polluting, no consent required, e.g. solar generation, electric motor repair)
Blue (2025, essential environmental services infrastructure designation)
categorization_pollution_index.scoring_basis: 0-100 Pollution Index combining air/water/waste pollution potential, equal weighting since a 2025 revision. Fuel type is a direct scoring input -- coal/liquid fuel scores higher (more polluting) than PNG/LPG/CNG/electricity.
categorization_pollution_index.modeling_opportunity: A fuel-switch or efficiency lever that lowers Pollution Index score can shift an MSME to a lighter CPCB category, reducing monitoring/consent costs -- a second-order financial benefit not otherwise captured. See subsidies.json -> cpcb_compliance_downgrade_benefit.

gaps_and_flags: No official average factory floor area (m2) by MSME category found nationally -- would need state Industrial Estate / DIC data.
Employment figure discrepancy (250M vs 60M) unresolved -- flag both rather than picking one.
CPCB Category II PM limit (1200 mg/Nm3) not confirmed as current.
No Ministry of MSME dataset directly stating typical kWh consumption per MSME category -- use the World Bank/TERI figures above instead.
